sundar.6.cau1: Laṅkā is the home of hosts of demons; how could a good person live here? So Hanumān began to reason in his mind, and at that very moment Vibhīṣaṇa awoke.
sundar.6.cau2: He called the Lord to mind, saying Rāma, Rāma, and Hanumān was glad at heart, knowing him for a good man. I will make a point of making myself known to him; a good man brings no harm to one's work.
sundar.6.cau3: Taking the form of a brāhmaṇa, Hanumān spoke to him, and on hearing him Vibhīṣaṇa rose and came there. He bowed, asked after his welfare and said: Brāhmaṇa, tell me your story and make it clear.
sundar.6.cau4: Are you one of the servants of Hari? A great love is rising in my heart. Or else, are you Śrī Rāma himself, who loves the humble, come to make me blessed?
sundar.6.do6: Then Hanumān told him all of Śrī Rāma's story, and his own name. At this, both of them thrilled from head to foot, and remembering the Lord's many virtues their minds were lost in them.
sundar.7.cau1: Listen, son of the Wind, to how I live here: like the poor tongue among the teeth. Dear one, will the Lord of the Sun's line ever know me to be without a protector and be gracious to me?
sundar.7.cau2: My body is tāmasic, of the nature of darkness; I have no spiritual practice, and my mind has no love for the lotus feet of the Lord. Yet now, Hanumān, I have taken heart, for without the grace of Hari one does not meet saints.
sundar.7.cau3: It is because Śrī Rāma has been gracious to me that you have sought me out and shown yourself to me. Listen, Vibhīṣaṇa, to the Lord's way: he always loves his servants.
sundar.7.cau4: Tell me, what high and noble birth is mine? I am a restless monkey, lowly in every way. Whoever takes our name in the morning goes without food that day.
sundar.7.do7: Listen, my friend: lowly as I am, even on me Śrī Rāma has shown his grace. As he remembered the Lord's virtues, Hanumān's eyes filled with tears.
sundar.8.cau1: Those who know such a master and still forget him and wander about, how should they not be miserable? Telling thus of Śrī Rāma's many virtues, he found a peace beyond words.
sundar.8.cau2: Then Vibhīṣaṇa told him everything: how Janaka's daughter was living there. Then Hanumān said: Listen, brother, I wish to see Mother Jānakī.
sundar.8.cau3: Vibhīṣaṇa explained every means to him, and Hanumān, son of the Wind, took leave of him and set out. Taking the same form again, he went to the place in the Aśoka grove where Sītā was living.
sundar.8.cau4: Seeing her, he bowed to her in his heart. She sits on as the watches of the night go by. Her body is wasted, her hair is a single matted braid, and in her heart she repeats Śrī Rāma's virtues one after another.
sundar.8.do8: Her eyes rest on her own feet, her mind is lost in Śrī Rāma's lotus feet. Seeing Jānakī in such distress, the son of the Wind was filled with grief.
sundar.9.cau1: He stayed hidden among the leaves of the tree, thinking: Well, what am I to do now? Just then Rāvaṇa came there, dressed in finery, with many women.
sundar.9.cau2: In many ways the wicked one tried to win Sītā over, using conciliation, gifts, intimidation and division. Rāvaṇa said: Listen, fair-faced and clever one: Mandodarī and all my other queens
sundar.9.cau3: I shall make your maidservants; this is my vow. Only look my way once. Holding up a blade of grass as a screen, and remembering her most loving lord, the king of Avadh, Sītā spoke:
sundar.9.cau4: Listen, Rāvaṇa: does a lotus ever open in the light of a firefly? Sītā went on: Understand this in your mind. Wretch, you have no thought of Śrī Rāma's arrows.
sundar.9.cau5: Fool, you carried me off when I was left alone. Vile, shameless creature, have you no shame?
sundar.9.do9: Hearing himself likened to a firefly and Śrī Rāma to the sun, and hearing such harsh words, Rāvaṇa drew his sword and, stung with fury, said:
sundar.10.cau1: Sītā, you have insulted me. I will cut off your head with this hard sword. Otherwise, do as I say at once, fair one, or you will lose your life.
sundar.10.cau2: Rāvaṇa, the Lord's arm is as lovely as a garland of dark lotuses, and like an elephant's trunk. Either that arm will be around my neck or your dreadful sword. Listen, fool: this vow of mine is true.
sundar.10.cau3: Candrahāsa, take away my anguish, born of the fire of separation from Śrī Rāma. Your edge is cool, keen and fine. Sītā said: Take away the weight of my sorrow.
sundar.10.cau4: Hearing her words, he then rushed at her to kill her, but Mandodarī, Maya's daughter, reasoned with him and gave him wise counsel. He summoned all the demonesses and said: Go and terrify Sītā in every way you can.
sundar.10.cau5: If within a month she has not done as I say, then I will take my sword out and kill her.
sundar.10.do10: Rāvaṇa went back to his palace, while here a band of demonesses take on many hideous forms and terrify Sītā.
sundar.11.cau1: One demoness, named Trijaṭā, loved Śrī Rāma's feet and was wise in discernment. She called them all together and told them her dream: Serve Sītā and do yourselves good.
sundar.11.cau2: In my dream a monkey burned Laṅkā and slew the whole demon army. Rāvaṇa is riding a donkey, naked, his ten heads shaven and his twenty arms cut off.
sundar.11.cau3: In this state he is going towards the south, and it seems that Vibhīṣaṇa has gained Laṅkā. Śrī Rāma's sovereignty has been proclaimed through the city, and then the Lord has sent for Sītā.
sundar.11.cau4: I tell you this dream aloud: when four days have passed, it will come true. Hearing what she said, they all grew afraid and threw themselves at the feet of the daughter of Janaka.
sundar.11.do11: Then they all went off this way and that, and Sītā thought anxiously: When the month is over, the vile demon will kill me.
sundar.12.cau1: Sītā said to Trijaṭā, her hands folded: Mother, in my misfortune you are my companion. Quickly find me some way to give up this body; this unbearable separation can be borne no longer.
sundar.12.cau2: Bring wood and build a pyre, and then, mother, set it alight. Wise one, prove my love true. Who could bear to hear words that pierce the ears like a spike?
sundar.12.cau3: Hearing her words, Trijaṭā clasped her feet and comforted her, telling her of the Lord's glory, strength and fair fame. Listen, gentle lady: at night no fire can be found. With these words she went back to her own home.
sundar.12.cau4: Sītā said: Fate has turned against me. I shall find no fire, and my pain will not end. Embers are plainly to be seen in the sky, yet not a single star comes down to earth.
sundar.12.cau5: The moon is made of fire, yet it does not shower fire on me, as though it knew me for an unlucky one. Hear my plea, Aśoka tree: be true to your name (Aśoka, without sorrow) and take my sorrow away.
sundar.12.cau6: Your new leaves are like fire: give me fire, and do not drive my suffering to its last extreme. Seeing Sītā so overwhelmed by separation, Hanumān felt that moment pass like an aeon.
sundar.12.so12: Then Hanumān, having thought it over in his heart, dropped the ring down to her. It was as if the Aśoka had given her an ember: she rose joyfully and caught it up in her hand.
sundar.13.cau1: Then she saw the lovely ring, engraved with Śrī Rāma's name and exceedingly beautiful. Recognising it, she gazed at it in wonder, her heart stirred by joy and sorrow together.
sundar.13.cau2: Who could defeat Śrī Rāma, the unconquerable? And no magic illusion could make a ring like this. While Sītā turned many thoughts over in her mind, Hanumān spoke in a sweet voice.
sundar.13.cau3: He began to describe Śrī Rāma's virtues, and as soon as she heard them Sītā's sorrow fled. She listened with ears and mind intent, and he told her the whole story, starting from the very beginning.
sundar.13.cau4: The one who has told this lovely story, nectar to the ears, why does he not show himself, brother? Then Hanumān came close to her. She turned her face away and sat, wondering in her mind.
sundar.13.cau5: Mother Jānakī, I am the messenger of Śrī Rāma; I swear it truly by the Lord, the treasury of compassion. Mother, I brought this ring: Śrī Rāma gave it so that you would know me by it.
sundar.13.cau6: Tell me, how did man and monkey come together? And he told her the story of how that companionship had come about.
sundar.13.do13: Hearing Hanumān's loving words, Sītā felt trust rise in her heart; she knew that he was a servant, in thought, deed and word, of the ocean of mercy.
